page: Microsoft Azure FX24-12mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 504.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 1417 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top 25%. Multi-core and memory bandwidth tests, including stress-ng multi-core and large-block memory read/write operations, fall within the average middle 50% range. For language model workloads, the processor achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models, but exhibits a performance tradeoff, dropping to the bottom 25% for text generation with medium 7B models.

The FX24-12mds_v2 offers a specialized resource density profile, combining high-frequency CPU cores with an exceptionally large memory footprint. This makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallelization across dozens of cores, but instead benefit from high single-core speeds and massive RAM capacity. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive database operations, caching layers such as Redis, text processing pipelines, and single-threaded data compression tasks.
